description.narrative:
Insatsen innefattar ett icke-öronmärkt stöd på 190 miljoner SEK till FN:s befolkningsfond (UNFPA) i Sydsudan för att implementera sitt landprogram under åren 2019-2022.
UNFPA:s landprogram för Sydsudan fokuserar på fyra mål.
1. Sexuell och reproduktiv hälsa och rättigheter:
Aktiviteter för att säkerställa att konfliktdrabbade befolkningsgrupper, särskilt kvinnor och ungdomar, får ökad tillgång till information och service inom t.ex. mödrahälsa, familjeplanering, könsbaserat våld och hiv-prevention.
Aktiviteter för att säkerställa att nationella system, särskilt för mödrahälsa och familjeplanering, stärks för tillhandahållandet av integrerad information om sexuell reproduktiv hälsa och rättigheter (SRHR) samt tillgång till relaterade service samt för ansvarsutkrävning avseende SRHR.
2. Unga människor:
Aktiviteter för att säkerställa att unga människor kan bättre fatta välgrundade beslut avseende deras SRHR och delta i planering, genomförande och utvärdering av fredsbyggande, utvecklings- och humanitära policyer och program.
3. Jämställdhet och kvinnors egenmakt:
Aktiviteter för att säkerställa ökad multisektoriell kapacitet för att förhindra och bemöta könsrelaterat våld och skadliga normer, inklusive barnäktenskap.
4. Befolkningsdynamik:
Insatser för att förbättra nationella system för generering och spridning av befolkningsdata och demografisk information. Detta ska även tillämpas i humanitära förhållanden.
Den totala budgeten för UNFPA:s landprogram uppgår till 90 miljoner USD. Andra givare inkluderar Norge, Kanada, Sydkorea och Schweiz.
UNFPA:s landprogram kommer till stor del att genomföras av ett flertal implementeringspartners (cirka 15 stycken). UNFPA kommer därför att vidareförmedla ungefär 60 procent av Sidas bidrag till implementeringspartners.
Omkring 80 procent av den totala budgeten är avsedd för genomförandet av insatser som är fokuserade på SRHR (det första målet).
I genomförandet kommer UNFPA även att samarbeta med övriga FN-systemet i Sydsudan, speciellt med UN Women, och andra givare inom ramen för givarfonden, Health Pooled Fund. Detta är betydelsefullt, speciellt eftersom Sida i nuläget arbetar med beredningar avseende eventuellt stöd till både UN Women och Health Pooled Fund i Sydsudan.

The UN Population Fund (UNFPA) in South Sudan has submitted a funding application to Sida regarding unearmarked support amounting to a total of 190 million SEK in order to implement its country program for South Sudan.
The UNFPA South Sudan country program focuses on four goals.
1. Sexual and reproductive health and rights:
Activities to ensure that crisis affected populations, particularly women and adolescent girls, have increased access to information and services regarding e.g., maternal health, family planning, gender-based violence and HIV prevention.
Activities to ensure that national systems, especially for maternal health and family planning, are strengthened for the provision of integrated information on sexual reproductive health rights (SRHR) and access to services and as well as for accountability on SRHR.
2. Young people:
Activities to ensure that young people are better able to make informed decisions on regarding their SRHR, and to participate in the planning, implementation and evaluation of peace-building, development and humanitarian policies and programs.
3. Gender equality and women’s empowerment:
Activities to ensure increased multi-sectoral capacity to prevent and respond to gender-based violence and harmful norms, including child marriage.
4. Population dynamics:
Activities to ensure improved national systems for generation and dissemination of population data and demographic information, including in humanitarian settings.
The total budget for the UNFPA South Sudan country program amounts to USD 90 million. Other donors include Norway, Canada, South Korea and Switzerland.
The UNFPA South Sudan country program will largely be implemented by several implementing partners (approximately 15). UNFPA will therefore forward about 60 percent of the Sida contribution to implementing partners.
Approximately 80 percent of the total budget is dedicated to the implementation of activities that are focused on SRHR (the first goal).
During the course of implementation, UNFPA will also collaborate with the rest of the UN-system in South Sudan, especially with UN Women, and other donors within the context of the donor fund, Health Pooled Fund. This is important, especially since Sida is currently assessing potential support to both UN Women and the Health Pooled Fund in South Sudan.

The UNFPA country program for South Sudan focuses on four outcome areas with five articulated objectives as presented below. Sida considers that the outcomes and objectives are clear and in line with the mandate and comparative advantages of UNFPA as the lead within the UN system concerning the outcomes and objectives. Sida also concludes that the outcomes and objectives are highly relevant for the South Sudan context and in support of the relevant Sida strategies i.e., clearly contributing towards their attainment. 1: Sexual and reproductive health and rights -Crisis affected populations, particularly women and adolescent girls, have increased access to information and services for maternal health, family planning, gender-based violence (GBV) and HIV prevention in emergency and fragile contexts. -National systems, especially for maternal health and family planning, are strengthened for the provision of integrated sexual reproductive health information and services and for accountability on sexual reproductive health and rights (SRHR). 2: Adolescents and youth -Adolescents and youth are better able to make informed decisions on their SRHR, and to participate in planning, implementation and evaluation of peace-building, development and humanitarian policies and programs. 3: Gender equality and womens empowerment -Increased multi-sectoral capacity to prevent and respond to GBV and harmful practices, including child marriage. 4: Population dynamics -Improved national systems for generation and dissemination of population data and demographic intelligence, including in humanitarian settings.

The UNFPA Country Programme (CP) 2019-2022 has contributed to better access to integrated sexual and reproductive health services and improved conditions to exercise reproductive rights, free of coercion, discrimination, and violence in South Sudan. Furthermore, the CP has contributed to improved gender equality, through increased multi-sectoral capacity to prevent and respond to gender-based violence and harmful practices, including child marriage. In addition, the CP has had a positive impact on national systems for generating and disseminating population data and demographic intelligence.
The UNFPA delivered on all five objectives under the four outcome areas. In addition, it should be noted that all output indicators except one were achieved and many greatly surpassed. This is particularly noteworthy given the many challenges faced during the implementation period, e.g., high levels of inter-communal violence and flooding, delays in enactment of relevant laws and policies, cultural barriers and negative attitudes towards SRHR-services, COVID-19 and inadequate data from government institutions to facilitate evidence-based planning.
Some key results include:
- 4 237 840 people were reached with integrated sexual reproductive health services (incl. family planning and GBV-response).
- 707 midwives were trained using a curriculum that meets the standards of WHO and the International Confederation of Midwifes.
- 74 secondary schools integrated sex education into the school curriculum and/or programmes.
- 13 One-Stop Centers were established within public health facilities for multi-sectoral case management of gender-based violence.
- 36 690 female sex workers were reached with the HIV Prevention Package of services.
- 182 520 Inter-Agency Reproductive Health and Dignity kits were procured and distributed to vulnerable women and girls.
- 5000 children and youth were directly engaged in activities focused on positive masculinity and preventative work to end GBV (with at least 20 000 people reached through social media).
In addition, the UNFPA worked on and advocated for the anti-GBV Bill, the Nursing and Midwifery Bill (both currently being reviewed by the Ministry of Justice), the Reproductive Health Policy (approved by MoH), the Family Planning Policy (set for validation through an upcoming stakeholders meeting) and a Youth Development Policy (to be submitted to the Parliament.
During the CP implementation, UNFPA also worked with traditional leaders, paramount chiefs and community leaders to collectively stand up against issues like child marriage and GBV. While it is difficult to establish causality, this is assessed to have contributed to all states and Administrative Areas having either passed or drafted laws, bylaws, declarations and/or resolutions against child marriages, GBV and early pregnancies during the Country Programme period.
Other noteworthy achievements:
Resource mobilization: UNFPA successfully mobilized the resources to achieve full financial coverage of the Country Programme budget. CP budgets tend to be ambitious and it is common that they have to be decreased during the implementation period. In a fragile and underfunded context like South Sudan, mobilizing the full amount can be considered a great achievement.
Nexus: UNFPA has successfully applied a nexus approach in all outcome areas throughout implementation. The key focus has been to foster greater coherence of programme activities to strengthen resilience and address the root causes of joint challenges. With a specific focus on SRH and GBV, UNFPA has enabled and encouraged coordination and collaboration to provide supplies, capacity building and information management across humanitarian, development and peace response efforts. The UNFPA has also worked on providing durable solutions through building capacity of national health service providers in Minimal Initial Services Package (MISP) in humanitarian settings as well as supporting the transition of services from temporary facilities to operational government health facilities. UNFPA also continued to support leadership, participation and capacity building of women groups, youth organizations and community structures in crisis recovery and post-conflict contexts to promote resilience and peaceful co-existence.
COVID-19: The context in South Sudan is volatile and the UNFPA Country Office has previously demonstrated their capacity to adapt and overcome changes in the context. This was put to test during 2020 and 2021 when the COVID-19 pandemic and the associated restrictions generated new challenges and needs while also delaying implementation of key programme activities. In addition to developing a Country Office Response Plan (in line with the National and UN-wide COVID-19 response), the UNFPA also integrated COVID-19 prevention measures and service delivery at targeted health facilities. UNFPA also monitored restrictions and developed plans to accelerate programme implementation once the restrictions had been eased.
Sidas flexible support to the Country Programme 2019 - 2022 enabled UNFPA to swiftly reprioritize and revise relevant workplans. Furthermore, the Country Office's readiness and willingness to assist with COVID-19 prevention and the spread of infection was an unexpected yet very welcome result.
Partnership with UNFPA:s Country Office in South Sudan:
The partnership between Sida and the UNFPA Country Office has worked well during the implementation period. The responsible programme manager at Sida, together with the sent-out staff member at the Section Office in Juba, has had close collaboration with the UNFPA focal point. In addition, Sida has actively participated (both virtually and physically) in the quarterly joint donor meetings with UNFPA together with representatives from Norway and Canada. The annual review meetings, implemented by UNFPA together with relevant ministries such as the Ministry of Health and Ministry of Finance and Planning were covered by the Section Office in Juba.
During implementation, Sida has joined on multiple field visits to programme sites. Some of these include the One-Stop Centre at Juba Teaching Hospital and health facilities in former protection sites turned IDP-camps. Sida also travelled in-country to visit programme sites, UNFPA staff and implementing partners in Rumbek and Wau (2021), Bor (2021) and Yambio (2022).
The visits have confirmed Sidas assessment that UNFPA is a skilled partner with the capacity to achieve the agreed results. The visits also reinforced Sidas understanding of the immense challenges and needs, both for immediate humanitarian support as well as long-term investments in health system strengthening.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
